newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-ARL APPOINTS NEW CHIEF EXECUTIVE.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-ARL APPOINTS NEW CHIEF EXECUTIVE.

text.p: The Australian Rugby League (ARL) on Wednesday appointed businessman Neil Whittaker as chief executive to lead its fight against media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's breakaway Super League.
Whittaker, 40, a former forward and captain with Balmain Tigers in the ARL premiership, replaced John Quayle, who resigned last month after 13 years in the job.
Rugby league in Australia, the world's strongest playing nation, has been divided into rival ARL and Super League camps during a bitter two-year power struggle.
The 10-team Super League, backed by Murdoch's global media empire, will kick off in Australia next year in direct competition with the 12-team ARL premiership.
ARL chairman Ken Arthurson described Whittaker as a proven leader with outstanding business acumen and an impressive career as a player behind him.
Whittaker played for Balmain between 1979 and 1985. He returned to the Sydney club as honorary president two years ago.
